corpus.title: Q3 numbers from Finance
corpus.text: Q3 revenue closed at $4.2M, up 18% from Q2. Enterprise renewals reached 94%, our best quarter yet. Churn was concentrated in the SMB tier, at 7% for the quarter. Marketing spend came in 6% under budget.

corpus.title: Q3 business review
corpus.text: Agenda: review Q3 results, agree the Q4 plan, and confirm hiring priorities. Leadership team and regional leads are attending. A pre-read is requested by Wednesday.

corpus.title: Q2 business review deck
corpus.text: Q2 goals were to launch self-serve onboarding and expand into two new regions. Self-serve onboarding launched in May. The pricing update was planned for Q3. Regional expansion reached one of the two regions.

corpus.title: Chat with Maya, your manager
corpus.text: Keep the QBR deck to ten slides. Lead with the renewal story. Be honest about SMB churn and what we are doing about it.

corpus.title: Leadership sync notes
corpus.text: The Q4 priority is efficiency. Hiring is frozen except for sales engineering. The pricing change moves to January. Partnerships need a clear owner.

corpus.title: Q2 strategy
corpus.text: We are making three bets: enterprise, self-serve and partnerships. The partnerships pipeline stands at 12 deals. Enterprise is the growth engine, and self-serve lowers acquisition cost.

corpus.title: 1:1 with Sam
corpus.text: Sam wants to own the onboarding project. Sam is worried about on-call load after the last two incidents. Follow up on the promotion timeline before the end of the month. Sam asked for a mentor on the data team.

corpus.title: On-call rotation
corpus.text: Five engineers share the on-call rotation. The last two incidents both landed on Sam’s shifts. A sixth engineer joins the rotation in November.

corpus.title: Northwind proposal
corpus.text: Northwind proposal: $48k per year with a 6-week setup. Includes SSO and a dedicated success manager. The contract term is two years.

corpus.title: Lumen proposal
corpus.text: Lumen proposal: $39k per year with a 10-week setup. No SSO until their spring release. Support is email only.

corpus.title: Brightline proposal
corpus.text: Brightline proposal: $55k per year with a 4-week setup. Includes SSO and 24/7 phone support. Pricing is fixed for three years.

corpus.title: Security team thread
corpus.text: Any new vendor has to support SSO before launch. Security review takes about two weeks.

corpus.title: Support assistant pilot results
corpus.text: The six-week pilot ran with 40 support agents. Agents using the assistant saved 3.5 hours per week each. First-reply time fell 22% during the pilot. Customer satisfaction held steady at 4.6 out of 5.

corpus.title: Assistant pricing from Relay
corpus.text: Relay quotes $30 per seat per month for the support assistant. Annual billing includes onboarding at no extra cost. The support team has 600 eligible agents.

corpus.title: Security review of the assistant
corpus.text: The security review found that the assistant keeps conversation logs for 30 days. Data residency in the EU is not supported yet. Security wants a signed data processing agreement before any rollout.

corpus.title: Agent survey on AI tools
corpus.text: 38% of agents worry the assistant will make replies feel generic. 61% of agents want help drafting replies to routine tickets. Senior agents asked for an easy way to turn suggestions off.

corpus.title: Analyst note on AI in support
corpus.text: Teams that adopt reply assistants typically see 15 to 25% faster resolution. The benefit depends on agents using the tool every day. A loaded support agent costs about $45 per hour.
